mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown three consecutive weeks of improvement before plateauing; absent a new shock, momentum in the recovering trend persists and the four-week forward mean stays at or above the trailing mean, continuing the gradual recovery trajectory already visible in the series.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -55.4 to -50.1 over t-3w to t-1w
failure_condition: Forward 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than the trailing 28-day mean, indicating the recovery momentum broke down rather than persisted.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week drop in WORKPLACES mobility exceeding 4 points signals a fresh tightening of restrictions or voluntary workplace withdrawal that quickly spills into reduced commute-linked retail visits, pulling RETAIL_REC lower within one week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 4 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -42.6 to -46.6 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat in the week immediately following a WORKPLACES drop of more than 4 points.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous stalling of TRANSIT and acceleration of WORKPLACES decline jointly indicate a broader contraction in out-of-home mobility infrastructure use; their combined weakening compounds to suppress retail footfall more than either series alone would predict, acting over a two-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change near zero or negative while WORKPLACES declines simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -50.7 to -52.0 while WORKPLACES fell from -40.4 to -46.6 over the same two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves over two weeks despite concurrent TRANSIT stalling and WORKPLACES decline, showing no compounding suppression effect.

mechanism_narrative: An uptick in RESIDENTIAL mobility after three weeks of decline is an early marker of renewed stay-at-home behavior consistent with tightening regime conditions; under this regime, retail mobility is predicted to fall over the following two weeks as households reduce non-essential outings.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 13.7 to 15.6 between t-1w and t-0w after declining for two prior weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next two weeks despite the RESIDENTIAL uptick, indicating the residential signal does not predict reduced retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM mobility (worsening percent change, i.e., increasing deviation toward baseline recovery reversal) reflects households shifting trips toward essential-only categories, substituting away from discretionary retail visits and depressing RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM worsens by more than 3 points week-on-week while RETAIL_REC stalls
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM worsened from -19.7 to -23.3 while RETAIL_REC barely moved from -50.1 to -50.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week following a GROCERY_PHARM worsening of more than 3 points, contradicting the substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained improvement in PARKS mobility over four consecutive weeks reflects a seasonal shift toward outdoor activity that typically co-occurs with broader non-essential mobility recovery, including retail and recreation visits, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved steadily from -80.3 to -75.4 across all four observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days even as PARKS continues its improving trend, showing decoupling of seasonal outdoor recovery from retail mobility.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES mobility declines for two consecutive weeks while TRANSIT also fails to improve, this combination signals renewed mobility restrictions specifically targeting commuting infrastructure, which within two weeks reduces linked retail trips made during commute routes.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES declines for two consecutive weeks AND TRANSIT does not improve over the same period
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined in t-1w and t-0w while TRANSIT stayed near -50.9 to -52.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the subsequent two weeks despite the joint WORKPLACES-TRANSIT weakening pattern.

mechanism_narrative: The co-movement of improving PARKS and improving RETAIL_REC over the trailing three weeks indicates a shared underlying driver of general outdoor and discretionary mobility recovery; continuation of PARKS improvement over the next four weeks will be accompanied by continued RETAIL_REC improvement.
evidence_refs: fact:Both PARKS and RETAIL_REC improved together from t-3w to t-1w
failure_condition: PARKS continues to improve while RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days, breaking the assumed co-movement relationship.
